name: Venus Legacy
lead: Venus Legacy is a clinic-based radiofrequency (RF) device from Venus Concept used for non-surgical skin tightening, wrinkle softening, cellulite smoothing and body contouring. People have it done to firm lax skin on the face, neck, arms, abdomen and thighs without surgery or recovery time, and treatments are given in a series of sessions.[1][2][6]

The device is the second generation of the Venus Freeze platform. Venus Freeze, launched in North America in 2011, pairs multipolar RF with pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMF); Venus Legacy, introduced around 2013, adds a larger applicator, variable suction and real-time thermal feedback.[6] A 2015 article in the Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology presented both devices as newer entries in the noninvasive RF skin-tightening trend.[3]

Published evidence on the platform is limited: the 2015 overview is based on before-and-after case series and was written by an author disclosed as a consultant and speaker for the manufacturer, and registered studies include a 10-person flank study combining cryolipolysis with Venus Legacy technology and a 50-person study of RF plus PEMF after liposuction.[4][5][6]

paras: Venus Legacy combines multipolar RF with pulsed electromagnetic field energy and variable-level pulsed suction, and is described as treating laxity, wrinkles, cellulite and mild fat reduction on the face and body.[2][6] Wikipedia lists Venus Legacy and Venus Freeze Plus as Venus Concept's RF devices among commercial skin-tightening systems.[1]

The 2015 overview describes the Legacy as having a larger applicator than Freeze, a vacuum (negative-pressure) component and real-time temperature feedback intended to keep tissue within a target range; it adds that wider electrode spacing is theorized to reach deeper tissue.[6]

RF energy heats the dermis and hypodermis. The 2015 article explains that this heat is thought to trigger collagen shrinkage, stimulate collagen and elastin synthesis and increase breakdown of fat cells, while the PEMF component is described as acting through non-thermal effects on collagen production and blood vessel formation, resembling a wound-healing response.[6] The suction is linked by the author to the gate-control theory of pain, in which a non-painful stimulus reduces pain perception.[6]
The article cites general PEMF research, including in vitro and animal studies, rather than trials of the Venus devices themselves.[6]

For Venus Freeze, the article describes applying a glycerine-based gel, choosing a handpiece, setting energy and moving the handpiece over the area until the target skin temperature is reached, with weekly sessions for 6 to 10 weeks depending on the area.[6] It describes the sensation as akin to a hot stone massage, with edema and erythema that resolve within hours and no downtime.[6]

Category-wide reports on RF devices include pain, dents from uneven healing, and rare fat necrosis or atrophic scarring.[1] Descriptions of the device list redness, swelling, burns and hyperpigmentation as reported effects, and pacemakers and pregnancy as contraindications.[2]

The 2015 Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology article presents four before-and-after case series for Venus Freeze (face and neck after 7 treatments, neck after 6, face and neck after 10, and arms after 4), without patient numbers, quantitative measurements or statistics, and reports no Legacy-specific data. Its author discloses a consulting and speaking relationship with the manufacturer.[3][6]

Registered studies on ClinicalTrials.gov include NCT02569112, a 10-participant study combining CoolSculpting with Venus Legacy technology for fat reduction and laxity of the flanks (started August 2015), and NCT03588702, a 50-participant study of RF and PEMF following liposuction (started July 2018).[4][5] Results of these registrations are not summarised here.

Venus Legacy is offered by aesthetic clinics under the Venus Concept brand and appears in combination protocols with fat-reduction devices and after liposuction, as in the registered studies above.[4][5] RF skin tightening in general is one of the most commonly performed cosmetic procedures, according to the 2015 overview.[3]

card.summary: Venus Concept's multipolar RF plus pulsed-magnetic-field device for skin tightening and contouring, with thin published evidence.
card.note: Evidence is limited to a short review and small registered studies.

quick.overview:
Venus Legacy is a clinic-based device from Venus Concept that combines radiofrequency, pulsed electromagnetic fields and suction. It is used for skin laxity, wrinkles and body contouring.

The published evidence found is a 2015 overview article and a couple of small registered studies.
quick.mechanism: Radiofrequency heats tissue to prompt collagen remodelling, with pulsed fields and suction added by the manufacturer's design.
quick.risks: Reported RF effects include redness, swelling, pain, burns and pigment change, and rarely scarring or fat loss. Pacemakers and pregnancy are listed contraindications.

chain: RF heats the dermis and underlying fat
Collagen contracts and new collagen forms over a treatment series
angle.text: Clients book a series of Venus Legacy sessions to firm skin and soften cellulite and fine lines. The handpiece is moved over the area until a target skin temperature is reached, with suction and pulsed fields added by design.
